ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Answer yes or no: Are proteins and glycoproteins the products of the viral replication process following 'process IV' as illustrated in the figure?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a schematic diagram of a viral replication process. After the virus enters the cell, structures such as viral RNA, viral DNA, viral dsDNA, mRNA, endoplasmic reticulum and vesicle are labeled in the figure. Label IV is located in the lower part of the cell, immediately after mRNA; from mRNA there is an arrow pointing to a group of small dot-like products, these products are located near the endoplasmic reticulum, and are connected to the subsequent endoplasmic reticulum/vesicle transport pathway. Reasoning: In the figure, process IV is located after mRNA formation, indicating translation of viral mRNA and related processing. Viral mRNA translation will produce viral proteins, and processing and transport related to the endoplasmic reticulum can produce or process viral glycoproteins. Therefore, the products after process IV can include proteins and glycoproteins. The answer is yes.
